questions.prompt: What is the difference between TypeScript's `private` and JavaScript's `#private`?

options.text: `private` is a compile-time check that's erased; `#private` is truly private at runtime

questions.explanation: private is a compile-time convention that's erased at runtime, so the field is still accessible then. #private is enforced by the JavaScript runtime.

questions.prompt: What does a parameter property do?

options.text: A constructor parameter marked with a modifier becomes a class field, declared and assigned automatically
It marks the parameter as static

questions.explanation: Putting public/private/protected/readonly on a constructor parameter declares and assigns the field in one step, removing boilerplate.

options.text: implements checks a class satisfies an interface's shape but inherits no code; extends inherits implementation from a base class
implements inherits code; extends only checks shape

questions.explanation: implements is a compile-time contract check with no inherited code; extends inherits a base class's implementation.

questions.prompt: Can you create an instance of an `abstract` class directly?

options.text: No — you must subclass it and implement its abstract members
Only if it has a constructor

questions.explanation: An abstract class can't be instantiated; it serves as a base that subclasses complete by implementing its abstract members.

questions.prompt: Under strict, the ______ check requires class fields to be initialized in their declaration or the constructor. (name of the option, one word/identifier)
questions.explanation: strictPropertyInitialization (part of strict) flags fields that aren't initialized, since they could otherwise be undefined.

questions.prompt: Match each class feature to what it does.

pairs.right: Belongs to the class, not instances
Non-instantiable base with members to implement

questions.explanation: static is class-level, readonly forbids later reassignment, abstract can't be instantiated, and #private is runtime-private.
